title: You, and your fathers from long ago.
subtitle: Old does not mean true

row.title: nothing
sub: an old mistake is still a mistake

then: Ibrahim widens the question: {idea}you and your ancient fathers.{/idea} They had said we found our fathers doing this. He answers that the age of the practice does not change what the idols are. {trap}A thing that never heard anyone did not start hearing because many people prayed to it.{/trap}
now: The family feud that started three generations ago. The way the men in your family talk to their wives because their fathers did. {trap}Something being old does not make it right.{/trap} You can be the one who stops it.
old: Something done for generations must have a good reason behind it.
new: An old mistake repeated for generations is still a mistake.
try: Name one pattern from your family you do not want to pass on. Do one thing differently today.

title: They are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds.
subtitle: Ibrahim's open, fearless break with idols
then: Ibn Kathir explains Ibrahim's words: {trap}if these idols have any influence, let them do me harm{/trap}, for I am their enemy and do not care about them. He compares it to Nuh and Hud saying {idea}plot against me, all of you{/idea}, and to Ibrahim asking how he could fear what they associate with Allah.
now: You are afraid that if you stop the lucky charm, skip the horoscope, or say no to the habit, something bad will happen. {idea}They have no power to harm you.{/idea} Only Allah does, and you are with Him.
old: If I cut off this thing I depend on, something bad might happen to me.
new: Nothing besides Allah can harm me, so I can let go without fear.
try: Let go of one superstition or false comfort today, and say: I rely on Allah.

title: He made me, and He shows me the way.
subtitle: The first reason Ibrahim worships Allah
then: Ibrahim says he will worship only the One who does these things. First: {idea}who created me, and it is He who guides me.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says He is the Creator who has decreed things and {reward}guides His creation{/reward} to them.
now: You are lost about the career, the move, who to marry. You read every article and ask every friend. {idea}The One who made you knows how you work.{/idea} Ask Him for guidance before you ask the internet.
old: Finding my path is entirely up to me.
new: The One who made me is the One who guides me.
try: Before your next decision, pray two units and ask Allah to guide you.

title: He is the one who feeds me and gives me water.
subtitle: Every meal traced back to its source
then: Second reason: {reward}He feeds me and gives me drink.{/reward} Ibn Kathir describes how Allah {idea}drives the clouds and sends down water{/idea}, reviving the earth and bringing out fruits, and sends water fresh and sweet for people and animals to drink.
now: You grab a sandwich between meetings and drink from a plastic bottle without looking at it. You think your paycheck bought it. {idea}Your paycheck is just the last step of a long chain that starts with rain.{/idea}
old: I feed myself with the money I earn.
new: Allah feeds me. My job is one of the ways He sends it.
try: Before your next meal, say Bismillah slowly and think of the rain that made it.

title: When I fall sick, He is the one who heals me.
subtitle: Ibrahim's careful words about illness
then: Ibrahim says {idea}when I am ill{/idea}, not when He makes me ill. Ibn Kathir says he attributed sickness to himself {idea}out of respect towards Allah{/idea}, and that no one can heal except Him, {reward}who heals with the means that lead to recovery.{/reward}
now: You are in the clinic waiting room with the prescription in your hand. Take the medicine, follow the doctor. {reward}And know who is actually doing the healing.{/reward} The pills are the means. The cure is from Him.
old: If I recover, it is because of the medicine.
new: I use the medicine, and I know it is Allah who heals through it.
try: The next time you take medicine, say: O Allah, You are the Healer.

title: He will cause me to die, then bring me back.
subtitle: Life and death in the same hands
then: Ibrahim says: {idea}who will cause me to die, and then bring me to life.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains He alone gives life and causes death, {reward}for He is the One who originates and repeats.{/reward} No idol could do either.
now: You get the call about a friend your age. Suddenly the deadline at work does not matter. {idea}Death is in His hands, and so is what comes after.{/idea} That thought can be heavy. It can also be the calmest thing you know.
old: Death is something to avoid thinking about.
new: The same Lord who gives me life will bring me back after death.
try: Spend one minute today thinking about death calmly, then do one good deed.

title: Even Ibrahim said: I hope He forgives me.
subtitle: Hope, not certainty, from the Friend of Allah
then: After listing what Allah does for him, Ibrahim says {reward}who I hope will forgive me my faults{/reward} on the Day of Recompense. Ibn Kathir says {idea}no one can forgive sins in this world or the next except Him.{/idea} The Close Friend of Allah still speaks with hope, not certainty.
now: You compare yourself to others: at least I pray, at least I do not do what they do. {idea}Ibrahim, the leader of the believers, said I hope.{/idea} Humility and hope belong together.
old: I am doing better than most people, so I am fine.
new: Even the best of people hoped for forgiveness. I should hope humbly too.
try: Tonight ask Allah's forgiveness for something you think is small.

title: Give me wisdom, and put me with good people.
subtitle: Ibrahim's first request for himself
then: Having described Allah, Ibrahim begins to ask. First, {reward}Hukm{/reward}, which Ibn Abbas said means knowledge. Then {reward}join me with the righteous{/reward} in this world and the next. Ibn Kathir links it to the Prophet ﷺ saying, as he was dying, O Allah, with the Exalted Companion.
now: Look at your list of duas. A bigger house, a better job, a spouse. Fine. {idea}Ibrahim's first request was knowledge and good company.{/idea} The people you sit with shape who you become.
old: My duas should mostly be about getting what I need in life.
new: Knowledge and good companions are among the best things to ask for.
try: Add one line to your dua today: O Allah, put me with the righteous.

title: Let me be remembered well by those who come after.
subtitle: Asking for a good legacy
then: Ibrahim asks for {reward}an honorable mention in later generations.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains: cause me to be remembered well after my death, so {reward}I will be taken as a good example.{/reward} Allah granted it: peace be upon Ibrahim is said to this day.
now: What will your kids say about you when you are gone? Your coworkers, your neighbors? {idea}Not a viral post. The way you treated people.{/idea} That is the legacy that lasts.
old: Caring about how I am remembered is vanity.
new: Asking to be remembered as a good example is a prayer Ibrahim made.
try: Do one thing today you would want your children to remember you for.

title: Make me one who inherits the Garden of Delight.
subtitle: The aim beyond the good name
then: Ibrahim asks to be {reward}one of the inheritors of the Paradise of Delight.{/reward} Ibn Kathir explains the pairing: {idea}bless me in this world with a good name after I am gone{/idea}, and in the Hereafter with the Garden.
now: You plan the pension, the savings, the five-year career goals. Good. {idea}Do you have a plan for the Garden too?{/idea} Ibrahim asked for it by name. You can too.
old: Paradise is something that will work itself out somehow.
new: Paradise is worth asking for directly and planning for.
try: Ask Allah today, by name, for Jannat al-Firdaws.

title: And forgive my father. He has gone astray.
subtitle: A son's love for a father who opposed him
then: Ibrahim prays: {reward}forgive my father, he is of the erring.{/reward} Ibn Kathir notes it was because of {idea}a promise he had made to him{/idea}, citing the verse in At-Tawbah, and that Ibrahim later stopped this when it became clear. That verse calls Ibrahim tender-hearted and forbearing.
now: Your father does not share your faith, or mocks the way you live. Some days you are angry. {idea}You can disagree deeply and still care, still hope, still be kind.{/idea} Ibrahim's love for his father did not disappear.
old: If my parent opposes my faith, I should cut off my care for them.
new: I can stand firm in my faith and still be a tender-hearted child.
try: Do one kind thing for a parent today, whatever your differences.

title: Do not shame me on the Day everyone is raised.
subtitle: Asking to be spared disgrace before all creation
then: Ibrahim asks: {idea}disgrace me not on the Day they are resurrected.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}protect me from shame{/reward} on the Day when all creatures, the first and the last, will be raised. He also reports from Al-Bukhari that Ibrahim will meet his father on that Day.
now: You would do anything to avoid embarrassment at work or in front of in-laws. You rehearse what to say, delete old posts. {idea}There is a Day when everyone will be there at once.{/idea} That is the shame worth preparing against.
old: What matters most is what people think of me now.
new: The shame I most need protection from is on the Day all are raised.
try: Quietly fix one hidden thing today you would not want seen on that Day.

title: The Day money and children cannot help.
subtitle: Everything people lean on, set down
then: Ibn Kathir explains that a man's wealth {trap}will not protect him{/trap}, even if he paid a ransom of an earthful of gold, nor his sons, even if he offered all people on earth. {idea}Only faith in Allah and sincere devotion to Him{/idea} will be of use that Day.
now: You work overtime to give your kids everything, and you tell yourself it is all for them. Good. {idea}But on that Day, they cannot carry you, and your account balance cannot either.{/idea} Invest in the one thing that crosses.
old: Providing for my family is enough to make me safe.
new: My family and money are blessings, not my ticket on that Day.
try: Give a small amount in charity today with the intention it is for that Day.

title: Only a sound heart gets through.
subtitle: The one thing worth bringing to Allah
then: Except {reward}one who comes to Allah with a sound heart{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says this means free from impurity and shirk. Ibn Sirin said the clean heart {idea}knows Allah is true and the Hour will come.{/idea} Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib said it is the healthy heart, the opposite of a diseased one.
now: You track your steps, your sleep, your cholesterol. You know your heart rate. {idea}When did you last check the health of your inner heart?{/idea} The grudges, the envy, the quiet doubts. That is the heart you take with you.
old: As long as my actions look good, my heart does not matter much.
new: What I bring to Allah in the end is my heart. Its health is everything.
try: Let go of one grudge today. Clean one corner of your heart.

title: Paradise is brought close to those who were mindful.
subtitle: The Garden comes to meet its people

row.title: those who strove
sub: and chose it over this world

then: Ibn Kathir says Paradise {reward}will be brought close to its people, adorned and decorated{/reward} for them to see. Its people are {idea}the pious who preferred it to whatever was in this world{/idea} and worked for it here.
now: You chose the dawn prayer over sleep, honesty over the easy lie, patience over the angry message. Nobody noticed. {reward}On that Day, the Garden comes to meet the one who made those choices.{/reward}
old: My small sacrifices go unnoticed and do not count for much.
new: Every time I choose Allah over this world, I am walking toward a Garden coming to meet me.
try: Make one small choice today for the next life over this one, and tell no one.
